reasons: No test for this file appears in the packet.
Every resize rebuilds the whole word layout and all pre-drawn pictures.
A pending font-loaded callback can still run after the component is removed.

terms.meaning: a rectangle on a web page that code can paint pixels onto
a small picture of one word, drawn once and reused many times
how many physical screen dots fit in one page pixel, used to keep drawing sharp
one picture the browser draws before each screen refresh
a system setting that asks apps to avoid movement
a built-in React function, such as useEffect, that runs setup and cleanup code for a component

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and file purpose
sections.what: Brings in the React effect and reference tools and describes the picture's purpose in a header comment.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code, though the header comment explains the intent.

sections.name: FRAGMENTS
sections.title: Word list shown in the plant
sections.what: The short schedule terms that get drawn as tiny words, such as activity codes, logic links and WBS steps.
sections.why: Likely reason: the words make the picture look like schedule data while staying generic.
sections.watch_out: Long words make sprites wider and change the spacing of the whole layout.

sections.name: COLOURS
sections.title: Colour palette and timing
sections.what: Lists the warm and cool colours for words and sets the full cycle to about 14 seconds and the sweep to about 11 seconds.
sections.why: Likely reason: sets the rhythm of the animation. The exact values are not explained.
sections.watch_out: The landing stylesheet runs the stage labels on a separate 14 second loop, so the two must be changed together to stay in step.

sections.name: Particle, Stray
sections.title: Shapes for words and strays
sections.what: Defines the data for one moving word and for one faint background word.
sections.why: Keeps each word's home position, colour and timing together so the animation loop can read them.

sections.name: drawSilhouette
sections.title: Silhouette shape of the plant
sections.what: Paints a plain white factory outline in a fixed design area: storage tanks, columns, a pipe rack, a building, a lattice tower and a wind turbine. The outline itself is never shown. It only guides where words go.
sections.why: Likely reason: a generic stand-in for a facility that reads as a plant at a glance.
sections.watch_out: All shapes use fixed coordinates, so moving one shape changes its relationship to all the others.

sections.name: seeded
sections.title: Repeatable random number generator
sections.what: Produces the same sequence of numbers each time from a starting seed, so the word layout is identical on every load.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the layout stable between page loads.
sections.watch_out: Changing the seed value changes the whole layout.

sections.name: buildSprites
sections.title: Pre-drawing word pictures
sections.what: Draws every word in every colour once, so the animation only copies ready pictures instead of drawing text each frame.
sections.why: Likely reason: drawing text on every frame would be slow.
sections.watch_out: Text is measured for size, so it must be drawn after the font loads. The code redraws after fonts load to handle this.

sections.name: buildField (part 1)
sections.title: Placing words and preparing the dots
sections.what: Walks row by row across the canvas, placing a word where the silhouette is solid. Words near the outline edge are kept only some of the time, so the outline looks softer. It also starts preparing the dot layer.
sections.why: Likely reason: softer edges make the silhouette look hand-drawn rather than hard-cut.
sections.watch_out: Random choices here decide how many words exist, so changing one step shifts the layout that follows.

sections.name: buildField: for
sections.title: Painting the dot layer
sections.what: Paints a fine grid of small dots shaped like the silhouette, with a few warm ones, so the plant reads from a distance before the words settle.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives a faint base picture that fades in first.
sections.watch_out: The dots are painted once at layout time, so any change to the outline needs the dots rebuilt too.

sections.name: CodePlant (part 1)
sections.title: Setting up canvas size
sections.what: Creates the canvas, reads its box size, sets its pixel size, and rebuilds the pictures and word layout whenever the layout runs.
sections.why: Likely reason: the canvas must match real screen pixels to look sharp.
sections.watch_out: Pixel density is capped at 2, which limits memory on very high-density screens at the cost of some sharpness.

sections.name: CodePlant (part 2)
sections.title: Drawing one animation frame
sections.what: On each frame, paints the dots, the faint background words, then each word moving from its scattered start to its home. Words brighten where the sweep passes and where the pointer is close.
sections.why: Likely reason: makes the build-up and the hover response feel alive. The exact values are not explained.
sections.watch_out: Every frame loops over all words, so adding many more words slows every frame.

sections.name: CodePlant (part 3)
sections.title: Animation loop, resizing and cleanup
sections.what: Starts the loop, pauses it when the canvas is off screen or the tab is hidden, rebuilds on resize, follows the pointer, and removes its listeners when the component leaves the page.
sections.why: Likely reason: avoids wasted work when no one can see the animation, and prevents leftover listeners.
sections.watch_out: Any new listener or observer must also be removed in the cleanup part, or it keeps running after the page changes.

summary: Draws the animated plant skyline on the landing page: a field of tiny schedule words that settles into a factory silhouette, with a warm highlight that sweeps across it.
purpose: Gives the landing page a decorative visual that hints at the app's idea (schedules turned into a model) without showing any real project data.
why: Likely reason: a decorative canvas keeps the page lively without needing real data. The reason for the fixed timings is not stated in the code.
how: First it paints a plain silhouette offscreen and reads its pixels to find where words and dots belong. It then places words inside the shape, paints a faint dot layer, and pre-draws each word in each colour. On every animation frame it draws the dots, faint background words, and then each word moving from a scattered start to its home, with a sweep highlight. Resizing rebuilds everything. Users who ask for reduced motion get one still picture.
inputs: The size of the box the canvas occupies, the screen pixel density, the reduced-motion browser setting, the mouse pointer position, whether the canvas is on screen, and whether the tab is hidden.
outputs: Pixels drawn on one canvas element. No data is saved or sent anywhere.
risks: Resizing rebuilds thousands of word pictures and the full layout, which can stutter on slow devices. The font-loaded callback is not cancelled when the component is removed. Stray words respawn with Math.random, so their paths differ each run.
debug: If the canvas is blank, check that it has a size and that the drawing context exists. If it stutters, check how often resize events fire. If the sweep or timing looks wrong, check the timing constants near the top of the file. If it keeps animating while hidden, check the visibility flags.
